To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BDAC is a hierarchical model, and its impact on firm performance is moderated by analytics capability–business alignment.

BDAC is a hierarchical model consisting of three dimensions, which are management, technology, talent capability, and 11 sub-dimensions, which are planning, investment, control, connectivity and compatibility, modularity and technology management, technical, business, and relational knowledge, and that BDAC is positively related to FPER and the relationship is stronger when analytics capability and business strategies are aligned.
big data analytics capability is a higher-order construct that consists of three primary capabilities and 11 subcapabilties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of BDAC and its impact on firm performance.
the question of how to develop and use big data to improve firm performance.
the development of a BDAC model, which can help managers better understand the nature and impact of BDAC on FPER.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BDAC has a positive impact on FPER, but the impact is contingent on the alignment of analytics capability with the business strategy of the organization.
the entanglement of the higher-order model of BDAC and business strategy alignment can significantly impact firm performance.
the higher-order BD AC model and its subdimensions, which is grounded in RBT and entanglement sociomaterialism, can be used to enhance firm performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a firm can achieve a high level of FPER through a well-developed BDAC.
the BDAC model can be used to guide the design, development, deployment, and management of BDAC to improve FPER.
the higher-order BDCA model has a significant positive impact on firm performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BDAC model is a valuable framework for understanding the BDAC–performance relationship.
BDAC is a critical resource to achieve superior FPER, and the BDAC model is a hierarchical structure.
the entanglement of BDAC, business strategy, and FPER is critical to understanding BDAC and its impact on firm performance.
